data.summary: Acne & appendageal disorders · 30 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Hidradenitis suppurativa** (Acne & appendageal disorders)_

**Q1. Define hidradenitis suppurativa (HS).**
- Chronic, recurrent, inflammatory, debilitating follicular occlusive disease of intertriginous apocrine gland-bearing areas, presenting with painful deep nodules, abscesses, draining tunnels (sinus tracts) and scarring, usually after puberty (acne inversa)
- Diagnosis: typical lesions (nodules, tunnels, scars) + typical sites (axillae, groin, inframammary, perineal, buttocks) + chronicity/recurrence (≥2 episodes in 6 months)

**Q2. Pathogenesis.**
- Primary event is follicular occlusion (infundibular hyperkeratosis) → dilation and rupture of follicle → spillage of keratin/bacteria → intense innate inflammation (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-17, IL-23) → abscesses and epithelialised tunnels
- Risk factors: obesity, smoking (strong), mechanical friction, genetic (γ-secretase genes — NCSTN, PSENEN, PSEN1; ~30–40% family history), hormones (premenstrual flares), metabolic syndrome
- Follicular occlusion tetrad: HS, acne conglobata, dissecting cellulitis of scalp, pilonidal sinus

**Q3. Severity staging.**
- Hurley staging: I — single/multiple abscesses without tunnels or scarring; II — recurrent abscesses with tunnels and scarring, widely separated; III — diffuse/near-diffuse involvement with interconnected tunnels and abscesses across an entire area
- Others: IHS4 (nodules ×1 + abscesses ×2 + draining tunnels ×4), Sartorius score, HiSCR (≥50% reduction in abscess + nodule count without increase in abscesses/draining tunnels) — trial outcome

**Q4. Associated conditions.**
- Metabolic syndrome, diabetes, obesity, PCOS, inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's), spondyloarthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum (PASH/PAPASH syndromes), depression, anxiety, Down syndrome, Dowling–Degos disease (PSENEN), SCC in chronic gluteal/perineal HS (men, smokers)

**Q5. Differential diagnosis.**
- Furuncles/carbuncles (acute, not recurrent at same flexural sites, no tunnels), epidermoid/pilonidal cysts, Crohn's disease (perianal fistulae), lymphogranuloma venereum, scrofuloderma, actinomycosis, granuloma inguinale, Bartholin abscess, cutaneous TB, anal fistula

**Q6. Discuss treatment including biologics (PYQ).**
- General: weight loss, smoking cessation, loose clothing, antiseptic washes (chlorhexidine, BPO), pain control, psychological support, warm compresses, dressings
- Hurley I/mild: topical clindamycin 1% twice daily, resorcinol 15% peel, intralesional triamcinolone 10 mg/ml for acute nodules; oral tetracyclines (doxycycline 100 mg BD for 12 weeks)
- Moderate: clindamycin 300 mg BD + rifampicin 300 mg BD for 10–12 weeks; metformin, zinc gluconate, anti-androgens (spironolactone, OCP) in women; acitretin (men), dapsone
- Moderate–severe: biologics — adalimumab (160 mg week 0, 80 mg week 2, then 40 mg weekly or 80 mg alternate weeks — first approved), secukinumab (IL-17A), bimekizumab (IL-17A/F) — approved for HS; infliximab, ustekinumab, anakinra (off-label); JAK inhibitors (upadacitinib) in trials
- Surgery: incision and drainage (acute relief only), deroofing of tunnels (preferred for Hurley II), STEEP, wide excision with healing by secondary intention or flaps/grafts (Hurley III), CO2 laser excision; laser hair removal (Nd:YAG) reduces recurrences

**Q7. Histopathology.**
- Follicular plugging and dilatation, ruptured follicles with neutrophilic abscesses, granulomas, epithelialised sinus tracts, fibrosis; apocrine involvement is secondary

**Q8. Prognosis.**
- Chronic relapsing; marked impact on quality of life (DLQI often very high); early recognition (average diagnostic delay 7–10 years) and early systemic/biologic therapy prevent tunnels and scarring

**Q9. Diagnostic criteria (Dessau).**
- (1) Typical lesions — deep painful nodules, abscesses, draining tunnels (sinus tracts), bridged scars, double-ended comedones; (2) typical sites — axillae, groin, inframammary, perineum, buttocks; (3) chronicity and recurrence (≥2 recurrences in 6 months) — all three needed

**Q10. Severity scores other than Hurley.**
- Refined Hurley, IHS4 (International HS Severity Score = nodules + 2×abscesses + 4×draining tunnels; ≤3 mild, 4–10 moderate, ≥11 severe), HiSCR (≥50% reduction in abscess + inflammatory nodule count without increase in abscesses/draining tunnels — trial outcome), DLQI, pain NRS

**Q11. Medical treatment ladder.**
- General: weight loss, stop smoking, loose clothing, antiseptic washes, pain control, psychological support
- Mild: topical clindamycin 1%, resorcinol 15% peel, intralesional triamcinolone for acute nodules
- Moderate: doxycycline/tetracyclines 12 weeks; clindamycin + rifampicin (300 mg each twice daily) for 10–12 weeks; metformin (insulin resistance), anti-androgens in women (spironolactone, OCP), zinc gluconate; acitretin (men), dapsone
- Moderate–severe: biologics — adalimumab (160 mg week 0, 80 mg week 2, then 40 mg weekly), secukinumab (IL-17A), bimekizumab (IL-17A/F); infliximab off-label; JAK inhibitors under trial

**Q12. Surgical options.**
- Incision and drainage only for painful abscess relief (high recurrence); deroofing of tunnels (preferred office procedure), local excision, wide excision with secondary intention healing or flaps/ grafts, CO2 laser excision/marsupialisation, laser hair removal (Nd:YAG) to prevent new lesions

**Q13. Complications of long-standing HS.**
- Scarring and contractures, lymphoedema (genital), fistulae (urethral, anal), anaemia of chronic disease, secondary amyloidosis (AA — nephrotic syndrome), SCC in chronic gluteal/perineal disease (aggressive, men, smokers), depression, suicide risk, sexual dysfunction

**Q14. Explain the pathogenesis — follicular occlusion concept.**
- Primary event is infundibular hyperkeratosis and follicular occlusion → dilatation and rupture → release of keratin and bacteria into dermis → intense innate inflammation (IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-17, IL-23) → abscesses, sinus tracts (epithelialised tunnels), scarring
- Contributors: genetics (γ-secretase genes NCSTN, PSENEN, PSEN1 in familial), obesity, smoking (nicotine stimulates follicular plugging), mechanical friction, hormones (androgens, premenstrual flares), dysbiosis — apocrine glands are secondarily involved

**Q15. Describe Hurley staging.**
- Stage I: single or multiple abscesses without sinus tracts or scarring
- Stage II: recurrent abscesses with sinus tracts and scarring, single or multiple widely separated lesions
- Stage III: diffuse or near-diffuse involvement or multiple interconnected tracts and abscesses across an entire area

**Q16. What is the follicular occlusion tetrad?**
- Hidradenitis suppurativa, acne conglobata, dissecting cellulitis of the scalp (perifolliculitis capitis abscedens et suffodiens), pilonidal sinus — share follicular occlusion pathogenesis

**Q17. What syndromes include HS?**
- PASH (pyoderma gangrenosum, acne, suppurative hidradenitis), PAPASH (with pyogenic arthritis), PsAPASH (psoriatic arthritis), SAPHO; associations — Crohn's disease, spondyloarthritis, Down syndrome, Dowling–Degos disease (PSENEN), metabolic syndrome, PCOS

**Q18. Ultrasound in HS.**
- High-frequency ultrasound detects subclinical lesions, measures abscesses and tunnels (fluid collections, widened follicles, dermal pseudocysts), guides surgery and staging (SOS-HS score); colour Doppler shows activity

**Q19. Why is HS often misdiagnosed and delayed?**
- Mistaken for recurrent boils/ abscesses and treated with repeated short antibiotics and incision–drainage; average diagnostic delay 7–10 years; clue — recurrence at the same flexural sites, double comedones, sterile cultures, tunnels

**Q20. What is the role of antibiotics and their limitations?**
- Anti-inflammatory and anti-biofilm effects: tetracyclines (12 weeks) for mild–moderate, clindamycin–rifampicin combination (10–12 weeks) for moderate–severe, ertapenem IV (6 weeks) rescue for severe; high relapse after stopping; resistance concerns

**Q21. Adalimumab and other biologics — details.**
- Adalimumab: 160 mg week 0, 80 mg week 2, then 40 mg weekly (or 80 mg every other week) from week 4 — HiSCR ~50–60%; evaluate at 12 weeks
- Secukinumab 300 mg every 2–4 weeks; bimekizumab (IL-17A/F) — high responses; infliximab off-label; screen TB/ HBV; combine with surgery for tunnels (biologics don't close fibrotic tracts)

**Q22. What is deroofing and how is it done?**
- Under local anaesthesia, a probe is passed into the sinus tract, the roof is excised with scissors/ electrosurgery, the base (gelatinous granulation) curetted, and the wound left to heal by secondary intention — low recurrence, tissue-sparing, office procedure for Hurley II tunnels

**Q23. Pain management and quality of life in HS.**
- HS has the worst DLQI impact among skin diseases; pain from nodules/ abscesses — NSAIDs, paracetamol, intralesional steroids (triamcinolone 10 mg/ml for acute nodules — quick relief), gabapentin/ pregabalin for neuropathic pain, avoid opioids long term; psychological support, depression/ suicide screening, sexual health

**Q24. Lifestyle advice in HS.**
- Weight loss (bariatric surgery for morbid obesity improves HS), stop smoking, loose clothing, avoid shaving/ friction, antiseptic washes (chlorhexidine, benzoyl peroxide), zinc supplements, dairy/ brewer's yeast avoidance reported to help some

**Q25. Histopathology in more detail.**
- Follicular occlusion with infundibular hyperkeratosis, ruptured follicles with mixed inflammation (neutrophils, lymphocytes, plasma cells, foreign-body giant cells), sinus tracts lined by squamous epithelium, dermal fibrosis; apocrine gland involvement secondary

**Q26. HS in women — hormonal treatments.**
- Premenstrual flares, PCOS association; combined OCPs with anti-androgenic progestins, spironolactone 100–150 mg/day, finasteride 5 mg/day (post-menopausal or with contraception), metformin (insulin resistance) — useful adjuncts

**Q27. Differential diagnosis (expanded).**
- Furunculosis/ carbuncles, infected epidermoid/ pilonidal cysts, Bartholin's abscess, Crohn's disease (perianal/ genital fistulae, metastatic Crohn's), scrofuloderma, actinomycosis, LGV, donovanosis, granuloma inguinale, cutaneous TB, deep fungal infection, Fox–Fordyce disease, SCC in chronic HS

**Q28. Disease activity scoring — HS-PGA and Sartorius.**
- Hidradenitis Suppurativa Physician Global Assessment (6 levels: clear to very severe), Modified Sartorius score (counts nodules, fistulas, distance between lesions, Hurley stage per region)

**Q29. Surgery after biologics — timing.**
- Combine biologics to quieten inflammation then excise/ deroof residual tunnels and scars; continue biologic perioperatively (no increase in infection in studies) to reduce recurrence

**Q30. Paediatric HS — features.**
- Onset before puberty suggests premature adrenarche, obesity, endocrine disorders (precocious puberty, CAH); treat with topical clindamycin, antiseptics, weight loss, adalimumab approved ≥12 y; avoid tetracyclines <8 y

## Quick spotter facts
- Recurrent painful nodules + double comedones + tunnels in axillae/groin — HS
- Hurley staging; adalimumab, secukinumab, bimekizumab
- Deroofing for tunnels

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Hidradenitis suppurativa); North American/European HS guidelines. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
